source.name: Ticking a 'None of these' checkbox must clear the other answers in its group even when each checkbox has its own name

journey.title: Choose 'No symptoms' after ticking symptoms with the keyboard
journey.goal: Ticking the exclusive 'No, I do not have any of these symptoms' answer clears the symptoms ticked earlier

functionalJourney.title: Tick two symptoms with a pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Both ticked symptoms are submitted and no-symptoms stays clear

guards.title: Choose 'Do not contact me' after ticking a contact method
guards.goal: The exclusive answer in a shared-name group clears the method ticked earlier

plan.root_cause: The unCheckAllInputsExcept method selects checkboxes by name attribute instead of the exclusive group attribute, so clicking the exclusive 'No symptoms' checkbox does not uncheck other symptom checkboxes.
plan.repair_strategy: Update unCheckAllInputsExcept to select inputs by data-checkbox-exclusive-group when present, falling back to name attribute, ensuring the exclusive checkbox clears other options in the same group.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can now clear previously ticked symptoms when selecting the exclusive 'No symptoms' option, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).
functional_risks: Possible regression for checkboxes that rely on the previous name‑based selection when no exclusive group is defined; the fallback preserves existing behavior.
verification_requirements: After the fix, selecting 'No symptoms' after ticking cough and fever results in symptoms[cough] and symptoms[fever] being unset.
Selecting a symptom after 'No symptoms' should clear the 'No symptoms' checkbox (existing behavior).
Mouse interaction with the exclusive checkbox continues to work.
Non‑exclusive checkboxes retain their mutual‑exclusion behavior.
